# `rx` command reference — @chrismessina/raycast-harness 0.5.0

Pinned version: **0.5.0** (`rx-version.json`). Skills and hooks never call `rx` or `npx @chrismessina/raycast-harness` directly; every call goes through the runner, which runs this exact version and appends the plugin preset to every preset-aware command:

```
node "<plugin>/scripts/rx.mjs" <command> [subcommand] [arguments] [--flags] [--json]
```

Global flags, which every command accepts and which are not repeated per command: `--json`, `--format`, `--help`.

`--json` prints one JSON envelope: `command`, `version`, `fingerprint`, `data`, `results[]`, `exit`. Verdicts are `PASS`, `FAIL`, `WARN`, `N/A`, `ERROR`; exit 0 = no FAIL/ERROR, 1 = any FAIL, 2 = any ERROR. Any unknown argument is `ERROR args` (exit 2). The dispatcher's own ids (`args`, `root`, `input`, `tooling`, `github`, `npm`, `git`, `protocol`, `internal`) may appear on any command and are not listed per command. A check id ending in `*` declares a prefix.

Commands (21): [`api-diff`](#rx-api-diff), [`api-floor`](#rx-api-floor), [`audit`](#rx-audit), [`changelog`](#rx-changelog), [`commands`](#rx-commands), [`contributions`](#rx-contributions), [`doctor`](#rx-doctor), [`gates`](#rx-gates), [`greptile`](#rx-greptile), [`guard`](#rx-guard), [`holdout`](#rx-holdout), [`judge`](#rx-judge), [`png`](#rx-png), [`post-merge`](#rx-post-merge), [`pr`](#rx-pr), [`preflight`](#rx-preflight), [`preset`](#rx-preset), [`publication`](#rx-publication), [`scan`](#rx-scan), [`shortcuts`](#rx-shortcuts), [`stale`](#rx-stale).

## `rx api-diff`

what changed between two published @raycast/api versions: file inventory, types/index.d.ts diff, CLI surface

Synopsis: `rx api-diff <from> <to> [--out <dir>] [--json]`

- Root: none
- Network: required: `npm view @raycast/api time --json`, then `npm pack @raycast/api@<v> --pack-destination <tmp>` for both versions
- State: none; without --out the packages go to a temp dir removed on every exit path
- Preset: not accepted

Arguments:

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `<from>` | yes | an exact published version, e.g. 2.10.1 (not a range, tag or latest) |
| `<to>` | yes | an exact published version; either order, the earlier-published one is the baseline |

Flags:

| Flag | Value | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--out` | `<dir>` | no | extract both packages to <dir>/<version>/package/ and leave them; never overwrites |

Check ids:

| Id | Description | Levels |
|---|---|---|
| `api-diff-window` | <from> and <to> are adjacent in publish order (WARN with the intermediate versions) | PASS, WARN |
| `api-diff` | the release inventory and declarations diff (N/A when only version fields changed; ERROR on any pack, extraction or read failure) | PASS, N/A, ERROR |

Data (`--json` → `data`):

- `package` — "@raycast/api"
- `from` — string — the earlier-published version (the baseline)
- `to` — string
- `published` — { from: string, to: string } — npm time entries
- `window` — string[] — versions published strictly between, publish order
- `dirs` — { from: string, to: string } | null — the extracted package/ dirs, only with --out
- `files` — { added: string[], removed: string[], changed: [{ path, fromBytes, toBytes, versionOnly }] } — paths relative to package/, sorted
- `versionOnly` — boolean — nothing added or removed and every changed file versionOnly
- `declarations` — { path: "types/index.d.ts", changed: boolean, added: number, removed: number, diff: string }
- `distTypes` — { added: string[], removed: string[], changed: string[] } — paths under dist/types/
- `cli` — { commandsAdded: string[], commandsRemoved: string[], flagsAdded: [{ command, flag }], flagsRemoved: [{ command, flag }], changed: [{ path, from, to }] } — oclif.manifest.json; changed holds every other differing leaf under commands, dotted paths, sorted

## `rx api-floor`

check @raycast/api (lockfile and manifest) against the preset's dependency floors; npm currency is advisory

Synopsis: `rx api-floor [--root <dir>] --preset <file> [--json]`

- Root: required
- Network: optional: `npm view @raycast/api version` for the currency advisory; unreachable → N/A api-currency, the floor checks still run
- State: reads repo/stale/baseline.json (written by rx stale) for the publication status
- Preset: preset-aware; the runner appends `--preset`

Flags:

| Flag | Value | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--root` | `<dir>` | no | extension root |
| `--preset` | `<file>` | yes | preset JSON holding dependencies.api |

Check ids:

| Id | Description | Levels |
|---|---|---|
| `api-floor-lockfile` | lockfile-resolved @raycast/api ≥ the selected policy's floor | PASS, FAIL |
| `api-floor-manifest` | the manifest range's lower bound ≥ the floor (WARN below; WARN when no range) | PASS, WARN |
| `api-floor-new` | a brand-new extension (rx stale: published false) is on 2.x | PASS, FAIL, N/A |
| `api-currency` | lockfile-resolved @raycast/api equals npm latest (WARN behind; N/A npm unreachable) | PASS, WARN, N/A |

Data (`--json` → `data`):

- `policy` — "existing-1x" | "2x"
- `floor` — string
- `resolved` — string — lockfile-resolved @raycast/api
- `range` — string | null — the manifest range
- `latest` — string | null — npm latest, null when unreachable
- `publication` — "new" | "existing" | "unknown"

## `rx audit`

record (validate and write) or show the agent audit that rx guard requires beside the gates receipt

- Root: required
- Network: none
- State: record deletes then writes repo/audit.json (attested with the rx key, created on first need at $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/raycast-harness/attest.key) and reads repo/receipt.json (its attestation, subject, generation and fingerprint), the root's generation file under $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/raycast-harness/generations/ and repo/stale/baseline.json; rotates nothing; show reads the same and creates nothing

Subcommands: `record`, `show`.

Flags:

| Flag | Value | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--root` | `<dir>` | no | extension root |

### `rx audit record`

validate the entries against the preset and the current gates run, embed the shortcut and png evidence, write repo/audit.json

Synopsis: `rx audit record [--root <dir>] --preset <file> --entries <file> [--extension-typescript] [--json]`

- Root: required
- Network: none
- State: record deletes then writes repo/audit.json (attested with the rx key, created on first need at $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/raycast-harness/attest.key) and reads repo/receipt.json (its attestation, subject, generation and fingerprint), the root's generation file under $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/raycast-harness/generations/ and repo/stale/baseline.json; rotates nothing; show reads the same and creates nothing
- Preset: preset-aware; the runner appends `--preset`

Flags:

| Flag | Value | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--root` | `<dir>` | no | extension root |
| `--preset` | `<file>` | yes | preset JSON: rule ids, applicability and severity |
| `--entries` | `<file>` | yes | JSON array of rule entries, dispositions and verifications (see src/audit/entries.mjs); must live outside the extension root |
| `--extension-typescript` | — | no | read the embedded shortcut evidence with the extension's installed typescript, which loads and runs that package's code (as rx gates' build already did); without it the shortcut step is the text scan and runs no extension code |

Check ids:

| Id | Description | Levels |
|---|---|---|
| `audit-coverage` | one entry per applicable preset rule and Greptile judgment rule (FAIL naming the missing ids) | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A, ERROR (default) |
| `audit-*` | audit-<rule id>: a rule whose entry says fail (FAIL for a block rule, WARN for a report rule) | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A, ERROR (default) |
| `audit-dispositions` | every stale CHECK / NEW? / REMOVE / DELETED path and png OLDER-SHOT / UNDECIDED image in this run has a disposition matching { path, localHash, baseline } (REMOVE and DELETED: localHash "absent", disposition remove-published, which no other row accepts) | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A, ERROR (default) |
| `audit-verification` | a destination / runtime verification entry per external effect the extension has (writes files, web requests, Raycast AI) | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A, ERROR (default) |
| `audit-greptile-rules` | ERROR when the Greptile rules in use changed while the audit was being recorded (another rx greptile update finished mid-recording); nothing is written | ERROR |
| `audit-receipt` | ERROR when there is no current receipt (missing, not attested by this machine's key, malformed, written for another checkout or an earlier gates attempt, its fingerprints no longer match the tree, it records a FAIL/ERROR, it was written with a different preset, or its greptileRules are not the Greptile rules in use) | ERROR |
| `attest-key` | ERROR when the attestation key exists but is unusable (not a regular file, not 32 bytes, accessible to group or other), or its directory exists with group or other access; rx never replaces the key or chmods a directory it did not create | ERROR |
| `shortcut-runtime-table` | a Keyboard.Shortcut.Common table from the running Raycast app is available (ERROR runtime evidence unavailable when shortcuts are declared and none matches; N/A only when none are declared) | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A, ERROR (default) |
| `shortcut-ambiguous` | no two actions in one resolved ActionPanel (or one toast) share a binding on a declared platform; one FAIL per conflicting pair | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A, ERROR (default) |
| `shortcut-reserved` | no ActionPanel shortcut spells out a binding its view's panel assigns itself (↵ and ⌘↵ in List, Grid and Detail; ⌘↵ and ⌘⇧↵ in Form); one FAIL per site and distinct binding, or a WARN when rx cannot see the view and the binding is a default in only some views; toast actions are not panels and are not checked | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A, ERROR (default) |
| `png` | one result per PNG under metadata/ or named as an icon in package.json; outcome in details[0] | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A, ERROR (default) |

Data (`--json` → `data`):

- `written` — boolean — audit.json written
- `fingerprint` — string — the receipt's combined fingerprint the audit is tied to
- `entries` — number — rule entries accepted
- `blocking` — string[] — every reason rx guard will block on (empty when the audit is clean)
- `reportOnly` — string[] — report-severity rules whose entry says fail
- `dispositions` — number — dispositions matched
- `applicable` — string[] — the rule ids that needed an entry

### `rx audit show`

print the recorded audit and whether it still matches the current receipt

Synopsis: `rx audit show [--root <dir>] [--json]`

- Root: required
- Network: none
- State: record deletes then writes repo/audit.json (attested with the rx key, created on first need at $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/raycast-harness/attest.key) and reads repo/receipt.json (its attestation, subject, generation and fingerprint), the root's generation file under $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/raycast-harness/generations/ and repo/stale/baseline.json; rotates nothing; show reads the same and creates nothing
- Preset: not accepted

Flags:

| Flag | Value | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--root` | `<dir>` | no | extension root |

Check ids:

| Id | Description | Levels |
|---|---|---|
| `audit-show` | PASS when audit.json exists, matches the current receipt's fingerprint and the Greptile rules in use, and has no blocking failure; WARN when it is stale or blocking, when the receipt's, the audit's and the current Greptile rules do not all agree (the guard's sentence), or when the receipt's or the audit's provenance fails (the guard's sentence); N/A when none is recorded | PASS, WARN, N/A |

Data (`--json` → `data`):

- `audit` — the recorded audit.json, or null
- `receipt` — { present, fingerprint } for the current receipt

## `rx changelog`

check CHANGELOG.md: one placeholder on top, history unchanged against the published copy, bullets ≤ 280; --merge rebuilds it during a merge

Synopsis: `rx changelog [--root <dir>] [--published <dir>] [--redactions <file>] [--merge] [--json]`

- Root: required
- Network: none
- State: --merge reads MERGE_HEAD and writes CHANGELOG.md in the root; otherwise read-only
- Preset: not accepted

Flags:

| Flag | Value | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--root` | `<dir>` | no | extension root |
| `--published` | `<dir>` | no | the published copy (from `rx stale`); enables changelog-history |
| `--redactions` | `<file>` | no | JSON [{ heading, originalHash, replacementHash, forbiddenLine }] authorizing privacy edits to dated entries |
| `--merge` | — | no | during a merge: rebuild CHANGELOG.md from HEAD and MERGE_HEAD by heading structure, then check the result |

Check ids:

| Id | Description | Levels |
|---|---|---|
| `changelog-placeholder` | exactly one {PR_MERGE_DATE}, in the top entry | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A, ERROR (default) |
| `changelog-history` | dated entries byte-equal to the published copy except recorded redactions; N/A without --published | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A, ERROR (default) |
| `changelog-bullets` | each bullet ≤ 280 characters (advisory: WARN at most) | PASS, WARN, N/A |
| `changelog-merge` | with --merge: rebuilt from HEAD and MERGE_HEAD (PASS) or ambiguous boundary (ERROR, nothing written) | PASS, ERROR |

Data (`--json` → `data`):

- `placeholders` — number — occurrences in the (rebuilt) file
- `topHeading` — string | null
- `entries` — [{ heading, date, bullets, changed, redacted }] — changed/redacted are against --published
- `merged` — boolean — true when --merge rewrote CHANGELOG.md

## `rx contributions`

during a pull-contributions merge: is each conflicted file a real contribution, or the published copy coming back?

Synopsis: `rx contributions [--root <dir>] --published <dir> [--json]`

- Root: required
- Network: none
- State: none
- Preset: not accepted

Flags:

| Flag | Value | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--root` | `<dir>` | no | extension root (inside a standalone or monorepo checkout) |
| `--published` | `<dir>` | yes | the published copy of the extension (rx stale's publishedDir) |

Check ids:

| Id | Description | Levels |
|---|---|---|
| `contributions` | ERROR: no merge in progress, --published missing or empty, or a missing object (never silence) | ERROR |
| `contribution` | one per conflicted path: OURS-SAFE (incoming == published; PASS) or REAL-CONTRIBUTION (FAIL); N/A when nothing is conflicted | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A, ERROR (default) |
| `contribution-branch` | WARN when a leftover ext/<name> branch (or MERGE_HEAD) adds only raycastbot's CHANGELOG date stamp (proven by content); PASS otherwise, each rejected candidate's reason in details | PASS, WARN |

Data (`--json` → `data`):

- `extension` — string — the extension subtree relative to the repository top level ('' when standalone)
- `conflicted` — [{ path, outcome, ours, incoming, published }] — blob ids (null when a side lacks the path)
- `incomingTree` — { onlyIncoming: string[], onlyPublished: string[], differing: string[] } — MERGE_HEAD's extension subtree versus --published, both directions
- `leftoverBranch` — { name, commit } | null

Synopsis: `rx doctor [--root <dir>] [--json]`

- Root: optional
- Network: `gh auth status` and the greptile-rules check contact github.com; everything else is local
- State: reads the attestation key $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/raycast-harness/attest.key and the Greptile rules copies under greptile/rules/ in the cross-repo cache; creates nothing
- Preset: not accepted

Flags:

| Flag | Value | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--root` | `<dir>` | no | extension root (for the ray check) |

Check ids:

| Id | Description | Levels |
|---|---|---|
| `node` | Node version is 22.12 or newer | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A, ERROR (default) |
| `ray` | node_modules/.bin/ray present in the extension root | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A, ERROR (default) |
| `gh-auth` | gh is authenticated (network probe) | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A, ERROR (default) |
| `git-signing` | commit.gpgsign is on and a signing key is configured | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A, ERROR (default) |
| `raycast-app` | Raycast.app version readable from its Info.plist | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A, ERROR (default) |
| `attest-key` | PASS the attestation key is a regular file of 32 bytes with no group or other access (prints its mode and keyId) / WARN not created yet / ERROR present but unusable, or its directory is accessible to group or other | PASS, WARN, ERROR |
| `greptile-rules` | PASS the Greptile rules in use match raycast/extensions main (prints the copy's kind, sha and date) / WARN out of date (one detail per change; run rx greptile update) / WARN could not check (offline or gh unavailable) | PASS, WARN |

Data (`--json` → `data`):

- `node` — string — process.version
- `ray` — { found: boolean, apiVersion: string | null } | null when no root
- `gh` — { authenticated: boolean, login: string | null, detail: string }
- `signing` — { gpgsign: boolean, format: string | null, key: string | null }
- `raycastApp` — { version: string | null, path: string, installed: boolean, error: string | null }
- `attestKey` — { path: string, present: boolean, keyId: string | null, error: string | null }
- `greptileRules` — { inUse: { kind, repo, sha, committed, fetched, path, origin, pr } | null, liveSha: string | null, changes: string[], error: string | null }

## `rx gates`

keep the Greptile rules current, run stale → scan → preflight → api-floor → build → tsc → lint and write the receipt rx guard requires

Synopsis: `rx gates [--root <dir>] --preset <file> --forbidden <file> [--json]`

- Root: required
- Network: greptile-rules' (GitHub API via gh: the latest raycast/extensions commit touching .greptile/ on main, then its .greptile/ contents when that differs from the copy in use); stale's (GitHub API, git fetch of raycast/extensions); api-floor's optional npm read; `npm run build` and `npm run lint` do whatever the project's scripts do. Never installs packages
- State: rotates $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/raycast-harness/generations/<root hash>.json first, then deletes and later writes repo/receipt.json { fingerprints, inputs, results, steps, data, subject, generation, greptileRules, rxVersion, at, attestation } (only when no step FAILed or ERRORed); writes a new Greptile rules copy under greptile/rules/ in the cross-repo cache when the live rules changed; reads repo/stale/; uses the cross-repo upstream/ cache; creates the attestation key $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/raycast-harness/attest.key on first need
- Preset: preset-aware; the runner appends `--preset`

Flags:

| Flag | Value | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--root` | `<dir>` | no | extension root |
| `--preset` | `<file>` | yes | preset JSON (passed to stale, preflight and api-floor; its bytes are fingerprinted) |
| `--forbidden` | `<file>` | yes | forbidden-values file for rx scan (its bytes are fingerprinted) |

Check ids:

| Id | Description | Levels |
|---|---|---|
| `greptile-rules` | the Greptile rules in use are current (PASS current), were updated to raycast/extensions main (PASS updated), or could not be checked (also when the step's 30 s deadline expires), failed validation or could not be installed (WARN; gates continues on the copy in use and the receipt records it); ERROR only when no copy of the rules can be loaded | PASS, WARN, ERROR |
| `stale` | N/A when the extension is not published (no baseline to compare) | N/A |
| `stale-mine` | published == local HEAD for these paths (PASS) | PASS |
| `stale-check` | published == an older commit of these paths; WARN requiring an audit disposition | WARN |

| `store-description` | a new or changed package.json description is about 50 to 155 characters, ends with a period, has none of the shared filler, and names only listed platforms | PASS, WARN, N/A |
| `readme-dev-sections` | README has no Development, build-from-source, clone-and-run or project-structure section, nor a Scripts or Contributing section over contributor commands (the README is the Store page) | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A |
| `readme-links` | every relative link in README.md and docs/**/*.md resolves from its own directory to a file that ships | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A |
| `changelog-placeholder` | exactly one {PR_MERGE_DATE}, on the top changelog entry | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A |
| `script-utils` | AppleScript and JXA run through runAppleScript from @raycast/utils: no "osascript" string literal (an exec/spawn of the binary) and no run-applescript package under src/ (Greptile script-and-sql-utils) | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A |
| `failure-toast-helper` | parsed with the extension's TypeScript (--extension-typescript, as rx gates does): object-literal style: Toast.Style.Failure inside a catch block or first callback of .catch(), or in a function reached by one identifier call from those paths or passed by identifier as the first .catch() argument (lexically resolved local functions/arrows or named/aliased/default relative imports under src/, following relative barrel re-exports up to eight re-export edges with cycle detection); each style property reports once, syntax errors WARN as not fully inspected; without a compiler a text scan WARNs at most and labels its PASS; result toasts outside catch paths and progress-toast assignments pass; .then(ok, onRejected), object/class methods, namespace imports are out of scope; domain-action Failure toasts can be legitimate exceptions (Greptile failure-toasts) | PASS, WARN, N/A |
| `nested-review-config` | no nested Greptile config (.greptile/, greptile.json) at any depth would ship | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A |
| `pref-description-length` | preference descriptions within the preset's budget | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A |
| `pref-label-length` | preference labels within the preset's budget | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A |
| `logger` | the preset's logger package is a dependency, imported, with its checkbox preference declared | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A |
| `logger-verbose-copy` | the verboseLogging preference equals the preset's block, every field | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A |
| `logger-strict-redaction` | the strictRedaction preference equals the preset's block, every field | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A |
| `agents-md-paths` | every backticked repo path in AGENTS.md / CONCEPTS.md exists (repo file extensions only; <!-- rx-ignore agents-md --> exempts a line) | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A |
| `agents-md-scripts` | every `npm run <x>` in AGENTS.md / CONCEPTS.md is a package.json script (<!-- rx-ignore agents-md --> exempts a line) | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A |
| `agents-md-no-home-paths` | no home-directory path (a machine path under the user's home) in AGENTS.md / CONCEPTS.md | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A |
| `agents-md-symbols` | every backticked symbol() in AGENTS.md / CONCEPTS.md exists under src/ (<!-- rx-ignore agents-md --> exempts a line) | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A |
| `api-floor-lockfile` | lockfile-resolved @raycast/api ≥ the selected policy's floor | PASS, FAIL |
| `api-floor-manifest` | the manifest range's lower bound ≥ the floor (WARN below; WARN when no range) | PASS, WARN |
| `api-floor-new` | a brand-new extension (rx stale: published false) is on 2.x | PASS, FAIL, N/A |
| `api-currency` | lockfile-resolved @raycast/api equals npm latest (WARN behind; N/A npm unreachable) | PASS, WARN, N/A |
| `gates-tree-changed` | the payload, HEAD, publish range, preset and forbidden list are the same after the steps as before them (a build or lint that writes into the payload is a FAIL; no receipt) | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A, ERROR (default) |
| `gates-rules-changed` | the Greptile rules in use when the receipt is written are the snapshot the greptile-rules step reported and stamped (FAIL, no receipt, when another rx greptile update installed a copy while gates ran; ERROR when the rules can no longer be loaded) | PASS, FAIL, ERROR |
| `build` | `npm run build` exits 0 (first error lines in details on FAIL) | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A, ERROR (default) |
| `tsc` | `npx --no-install tsc --noEmit` exits 0 (first error lines in details on FAIL) | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A, ERROR (default) |
| `lint` | `npm run lint` exits 0 (first error lines in details on FAIL) | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A, ERROR (default) |
| `attest-key` | ERROR when the attestation key exists but is unusable (not a regular file, not 32 bytes, accessible to group or other), or its directory or generations/ exists with group or other access; rx never replaces the key or chmods a directory it did not create | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A, ERROR (default) |

Data (`--json` → `data`):

- `receipt` — string | null — the receipt path when written, null when a step blocked it
- `fingerprints` — { payload, head, publishRange, preset, forbidden, rxVersion, baseline, combined }
- `steps` — [{ name, exit }] — every step in run order with its own exit code (0, 1, 2)
- `greptileRules` — { repo, sha, digest } | null — the Greptile rules the receipt is bound to (null when they could not be loaded)

## `rx greptile`

fetch a Greptile round, wait for the next one, authorize a reply, or keep the Greptile rules current

- Root: optional
- Network: GitHub API via gh (raycast/extensions)
- State: greptile/<owner>/<name>/<N>/ under the extension's repo state when a root resolves, else under the cross-repo cache

Subcommands: `fetch`, `wait`, `can-reply`, `outdated`, `update`.

### `rx greptile fetch`

the current round: score, updated_at, last reviewed commit, the summary body, inline findings, PR head

Synopsis: `rx greptile fetch <N> [--root <dir>] [--json]`

- Root: optional
- Network: GitHub API via gh (raycast/extensions)
- State: writes rounds/<updated_at>.json in greptile/<owner>/<name>/<N>/ under the extension's repo state when a root resolves, else under the cross-repo cache
- Preset: not accepted

Arguments:

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `<N>` | yes | pull request number in raycast/extensions |

Flags:

| Flag | Value | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--root` | `<dir>` | no | extension root whose repo state holds the round store (optional; cross-repo cache otherwise) |

Check ids:

| Id | Description | Levels |
|---|---|---|
| `greptile-round` | a Greptile summary exists on the PR and was stored as a round | PASS, N/A |

Data (`--json` → `data`):

- `repo` — owner/name
- `pr` — int
- `head` — sha
- `round` — { score, updatedAt, reviewedCommit, summary, findings: [{ id, path, line, originalCommitId, body }] } | null

### `rx greptile wait`

one ETag-conditional GET: PASS new round / N/A no change / ERROR on any failure

Synopsis: `rx greptile wait <N> [--root <dir>] [--json]`

- Root: optional
- Network: GitHub API via gh (raycast/extensions)
- State: reads and writes etag and seen in greptile/<owner>/<name>/<N>/ under the extension's repo state when a root resolves, else under the cross-repo cache (fetch writes seen too, as the wait baseline)
- Preset: not accepted

Arguments:

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `<N>` | yes | pull request number in raycast/extensions |

Flags:

| Flag | Value | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--root` | `<dir>` | no | extension root whose repo state holds the round store (optional; cross-repo cache otherwise) |

Check ids:

| Id | Description | Levels |
|---|---|---|
| `greptile-wait` | a new Greptile round arrived (PASS), nothing changed (N/A), or the check could not complete (ERROR) | PASS, N/A, ERROR |

Data (`--json` → `data`):

- `etag` — string | null
- `changed` — boolean
- `updatedAt` — string | null

### `rx greptile can-reply`

authorize exactly these reply bytes on one finding of a stored round at an expected head

Synopsis: `rx greptile can-reply <N> [--root <dir>] --round <updated_at> --finding <id> --expected-head <sha> --forbidden <file> --reply <file> --evidence <file> [--claims-fix] [--json]`

- Root: optional
- Network: GitHub API via gh (raycast/extensions)
- State: appends to replies.json in greptile/<owner>/<name>/<N>/ under the extension's repo state when a root resolves, else under the cross-repo cache; reads repo/publication.json with --claims-fix
- Preset: not accepted

Arguments:

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `<N>` | yes | pull request number in raycast/extensions |

Flags:

| Flag | Value | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--root` | `<dir>` | no | extension root whose repo state holds the round store (optional; cross-repo cache otherwise) |
| `--round` | `<updated_at>` | yes | the stored round's summary updated_at |
| `--finding` | `<id>` | yes | the inline finding (review comment id) being answered |
| `--expected-head` | `<sha>` | yes | the PR head the reply is written against |
| `--forbidden` | `<file>` | yes | forbidden literals, one per line (blank lines and # comments ignored) |
| `--reply` | `<file>` | yes | the exact reply bytes to post |
| `--evidence` | `<file>` | yes | JSON { finding, disposition: fixed\|partial\|declined, artifact, explanation } |
| `--claims-fix` | — | no | the reply says a fix was published; requires repo/publication.json (written by `rx publication record`) for this PR at a new remote SHA |

Check ids:

| Id | Description | Levels |
|---|---|---|
| `reply-round` | the finding belongs to the stored round named by --round | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A, ERROR (default) |
| `reply-head` | the fetched PR head equals --expected-head | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A, ERROR (default) |
| `reply-evidence` | the evidence names this finding with a disposition consistent with --claims-fix | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A, ERROR (default) |
| `reply-publication` | a fix claim is backed by publication.json naming this PR at the current remote SHA, different from the reviewed commit | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A, ERROR (default) |
| `reply-scan` | the reply bytes contain no forbidden literal | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A, ERROR (default) |

Data (`--json` → `data`):

- `authorized` — boolean
- `record` — { repo, pr, round, finding, expectedHead, evidenceHash, forbiddenHash, replyHash, authorized, at }

### `rx greptile outdated`

compare the Greptile rules in use with the live .greptile/ on raycast/extensions main

Synopsis: `rx greptile outdated [--json]`

- Root: none
- Network: GitHub API via gh: raycast/extensions the latest commit touching .greptile/ on main, then its .greptile/ contents when that differs from the copy in use
- State: reads the cache copies in greptile/rules/ under the cross-repo cache; writes nothing
- Preset: not accepted

Check ids:

| Id | Description | Levels |
|---|---|---|
| `greptile-outdated` | the rules in use match the live rules (PASS), differ (FAIL, one detail per change), or could not be compared (ERROR) | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A, ERROR (default) |

Data (`--json` → `data`):

- `inUse` — { kind: updated|shipped, repo, sha, committed, fetched, path, origin: main|pr, pr }
- `live` — { source, sha, committed } | null
- `changes` — string[] (source moved included)

### `rx greptile update`

fetch the live .greptile/ from raycast/extensions main and make it the copy in use

Synopsis: `rx greptile update [--dest <dir>] [--json]`

- Root: none
- Network: GitHub API via gh: raycast/extensions the latest commit touching .greptile/ on main, then its .greptile/ contents when that differs from the copy in use
- State: writes a new copy under greptile/rules/ in the cross-repo cache, or with --dest only into --dest/src/rules/greptile/; nothing when already current or on error
- Preset: not accepted

Flags:

| Flag | Value | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--dest` | `<dir>` | no | a raycast-harness maintainer checkout whose src/rules/greptile/ receives the update instead of the cache (never the installed package) |

Check ids:

| Id | Description | Levels |
|---|---|---|
| `greptile-update` | the live rules were written and are the copy in use (PASS updated), matched already (PASS already current), were written to the cache but a copy from a later upstream commit stays in use (WARN, naming it), or could not be read, validated or written (ERROR, nothing written; --dest is restored all-or-nothing) | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A, ERROR (default) |

Data (`--json` → `data`):

- `previous` — { kind, repo, sha, committed, fetched, path, origin, pr } (the copy compared against)
- `live` — { source, sha, committed } | null
- `changes` — string[] (source moved included)
- `updated` — string | null (the directory written)
- `inUse` — boolean | null (whether the cache copy written, or the current one, is the copy in use; null with --dest)

## `rx guard`

PreToolUse hook: allow `ray publish` / `npm run publish` only behind a current, attested receipt and audit; always block `gh pr ready`; block writes to rx state and the attestation key

Synopsis: `rx guard [--json]`

- Root: none
- Network: none
- State: reads repo/receipt.json and repo/audit.json of the extension that resolves from the publish command's directory (the hook payload's cwd, or the one `cd <dir> &&` the allowed shapes admit), the attestation key $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/raycast-harness/attest.key and that root's generation file under $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/raycast-harness/generations/; creates nothing
- Preset: not accepted

Check ids:

| Id | Description | Levels |
|---|---|---|
| `guard` | PASS allow / FAIL block (with the one-sentence reason) / N/A not a guarded command or target | PASS, FAIL, N/A |

Data (`--json` → `data`):

- `decision` — "allow" | "block"
- `reason` — string — the sentence a block carries; "allowed" or why it was not a guarded command
- `command` — string | null — the Bash command examined (null for any other tool)
- `path` — string | null — the physical Write / Edit / MultiEdit / NotebookEdit target examined (null for Bash and other tools)
- `roots` — string[] — the extension root the publish resolved to (one element, or none when blocked before any state was read)
- `receipt` — { present, fresh, complete } for the root checked; null until a root check begins (not a publish, blocked before any state was read, or no root resolves)
- `audit` — { present, fresh, blocking } for the root checked; null on the same early returns as receipt

## `rx holdout`

move untracked local-only files out of the root before a publish (out) and restore them, verified, afterward (in)

- Root: required
- Network: none
- State: writes repo/holdout/inventory.json and moves files to repo/holdout/files/ (`git rev-parse --git-path rx`)

Subcommands: `out`, `in`.

### `rx holdout out`

move the preset's untracked local-only entries out of the root, recording an inventory

Synopsis: `rx holdout out [--root <dir>] --preset <file> [--json]`

- Root: required
- Network: none
- State: writes repo/holdout/inventory.json and moves files to repo/holdout/files/ (`git rev-parse --git-path rx`)
- Preset: preset-aware; the runner appends `--preset`

Flags:

| Flag | Value | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--root` | `<dir>` | no | extension root |
| `--preset` | `<file>` | yes | preset JSON, validated against the preset schema; reads holdout.localOnly and ship.keep |

Check ids:

| Id | Description | Levels |
|---|---|---|
| `holdout-out` | untracked local-only entries moved (PASS with one detail per path; N/A when nothing matches) | PASS, N/A |
| `holdout-tracked` | no local-only path is tracked in this checkout's index (FAIL names each one with its fix: git rm --cached <path>, the file stays on disk, and list it in the extension's .gitignore; ERROR, before anything moves or an inventory is written, when git cannot read the index) | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A, ERROR (default) |
| `holdout-inventory` | inventory written and non-empty whenever a movable local-only path exists (ERROR otherwise, or when a holdout is already in progress) | PASS, ERROR |

Data (`--json` → `data`):

- `moved` — [{ source, destination, type, hash }]
- `restored` — [] (always empty for out)
- `skipped` — [{ path, reason }]

### `rx holdout in`

restore every inventory entry without overwriting a changed destination, and verify each hash

Synopsis: `rx holdout in [--root <dir>] [--json]`

- Root: required
- Network: none
- State: writes repo/holdout/inventory.json and moves files to repo/holdout/files/ (`git rev-parse --git-path rx`)
- Preset: not accepted

Flags:

| Flag | Value | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--root` | `<dir>` | no | extension root |

Check ids:

| Id | Description | Levels |
|---|---|---|
| `holdout-in` | every entry restored to its source and verified by hash (FAIL names the path that changed or failed) | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A, ERROR (default) |
| `holdout-inventory` | inventory present and recorded for this root (ERROR when missing or for another root) | PASS, ERROR |

Data (`--json` → `data`):

- `moved` — [] (always empty for in)
- `restored` — [{ source, destination, type, hash }]
- `skipped` — [{ path, reason }]

## `rx judge`

advisory answers to named judgment calls (never blocks, never acts)

- Root: none
- Network: the chosen provider's API only (Jev: api.typesafe.ai with TYPESAFE_API_KEY; Haiku: api.anthropic.com with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY); agent mode: none
- State: none

Subcommands: `ask`, `eval`.

### `rx judge ask`

one decision for one set of inputs: a provider's answer probabilities, or the structured question in agent mode

Synopsis: `rx judge ask <decision-id> --inputs <file> [--provider <jev|haiku|agent>] [--json]`

- Root: none
- Network: the chosen provider's API only (Jev: api.typesafe.ai with TYPESAFE_API_KEY; Haiku: api.anthropic.com with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY); agent mode: none
- State: none
- Preset: not accepted

Arguments:

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `<decision-id>` | yes | one of src/judge/decisions/: changelog-user-visible, needs-code, png-provenance, review-finding-triage |

Flags:

| Flag | Value | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--inputs` | `<file>` | yes | JSON file validated against the decision's inputs schema |
| `--provider` | `<jev\|haiku\|agent>` | no | provider; default per D6: jev if TYPESAFE_API_KEY is set, else haiku if ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is set, else agent |

Check ids:

| Id | Description | Levels |
|---|---|---|
| `judge-inputs` | the inputs file is valid against the decision's inputs schema (ERROR otherwise) | PASS, ERROR |
| `judge-provider` | a provider error (missing key, HTTP error, timeout, malformed output); WARN, then agent mode in the same run | WARN |
| `judge-*` | judge-<decision-id>: PASS with data.answer when the top probability is at least 0.7, WARN defer-to-agent below, N/A in agent mode | PASS, WARN, N/A |

Data (`--json` → `data`):

- `decision` — string
- `mode` — "provider" | "agent"
- `provider` — "jev" | "haiku" | "agent"
- `answer` — string | null — set only on PASS
- `top` — { answer, probability } | null
- `probabilities` — Record<answer, number> | null — normalized to sum to 1; null in agent mode
- `probabilitySource` — "provider-reported" (jev) | "model-reported" (haiku) | null — never calibrated
- `latencyMs` — number | null
- `threshold` — 0.7
- `fallback` — { provider, error } | null — the provider error that sent this run to agent mode
- `prompt` — { question, answers, inputs } — agent mode and defer-to-agent only

### `rx judge eval`

run every fixture of a decision and report per-case output and accuracy

Synopsis: `rx judge eval <decision-id> [--provider <jev|haiku|agent>] [--json]`

- Root: none
- Network: the chosen provider's API only (Jev: api.typesafe.ai with TYPESAFE_API_KEY; Haiku: api.anthropic.com with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY); agent mode: none
- State: none
- Preset: not accepted

Arguments:

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `<decision-id>` | yes | one of src/judge/decisions/: changelog-user-visible, needs-code, png-provenance, review-finding-triage |

Flags:

| Flag | Value | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--provider` | `<jev\|haiku\|agent>` | no | provider; default per D6: jev if TYPESAFE_API_KEY is set, else haiku if ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is set, else agent |

Check ids:

| Id | Description | Levels |
|---|---|---|
| `judge-provider` | a provider error; WARN, then every fixture in agent mode | WARN |
| `judge-eval` | one per fixture: PASS when the provider's answer clears 0.7 and equals the expected answer, FAIL otherwise, N/A in agent mode | PASS, FAIL, N/A |
| `judge-accuracy` | the share of fixtures answered correctly; PASS when every fixture is (the adoption rule), WARN otherwise, N/A in agent mode | PASS, WARN, N/A |

Data (`--json` → `data`):

- `decision` — string
- `mode` — "provider" | "agent"
- `provider` — "jev" | "haiku" | "agent"
- `probabilitySource` — "provider-reported" | "model-reported" | null
- `accuracy` — number | null — correct / total; null in agent mode
- `correct` — number | null
- `total` — number
- `fallback` — { provider, error } | null
- `cases` — [{ index, source, expected, answer, top, probabilities, latencyMs, verdict }]

## `rx png`

triage screenshots and icons against the published copy: SAME-PIXELS, 16-BIT, UNDECIDED, LOCAL-ONLY, OLDER-SHOT, NOT-YOURS (read-only; UNDECIDED and OLDER-SHOT need an audit disposition)

Synopsis: `rx png [--root <dir>] [--published <dir>] [--json]`

- Root: required
- Network: none (reads git history locally)
- State: none (read-only; recommends, never modifies a file). A --published dir inside the upstream cache is read under the cache's reader lock (ERROR github after the wait if another rx holds it)
- Preset: not accepted

Flags:

| Flag | Value | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--root` | `<dir>` | no | extension root |
| `--published` | `<dir>` | no | the extension as published in raycast/extensions (same layout); without it every 8-bit file is LOCAL-ONLY |

Check ids:

| Id | Description | Levels |
|---|---|---|
| `png` | one result per PNG under metadata/ or named as an icon in package.json; outcome in details[0] | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A, ERROR (default) |

Data (`--json` → `data`):

- `published` — boolean — whether --published was given
- `files` — [{ path, outcome, local: { width, height, bitDepth, colorType, gAMA, iCCP, sRGB, cHRM } | null, published: {…} | null, provenance: string | null (commit whose blob the published bytes match, OLDER-SHOT only), localHash: "sha256:…" | null (null only when the local file is unreadable), baseline: string | null (OLDER-SHOT: same commit as provenance; UNDECIDED: "sha256:…" of the published bytes) }]

## `rx post-merge`

after raycast/extensions merges this extension's PR, adopt raycastbot's merge-time rewrites (CHANGELOG stamp, recompressed PNGs) in one signed commit and push it

Synopsis: `rx post-merge [<pr>] [--root <dir>] [--dry-run] [--json]`

- Root: required
- Network: GitHub API through the transport (the pull request, its commits, each raycastbot commit, two tree listings, the authenticated user and that user's SSH signing keys); the published-copy refresh (git fetch of raycast/extensions into the cache); git ls-remote and git push of the current branch's upstream URL
- State: reads repo/publication.json; refreshes cache/upstream/; creates the signing key on first need (never under --dry-run); without --dry-run writes the adopted blobs, a tree and the signed commit into the object database, then under index.lock sets the adopted paths' index entries (keeping every other entry), writes the adopted files into the payload and moves the current branch by one commit (update-ref against its old value), then pushes that commit; writes no repo state of its own; under --dry-run writes nothing outside the cache
- Preset: not accepted

Arguments:

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `<pr>` | no | pull request number in raycast/extensions (default: repo/publication.json's pr when its repo is raycast/extensions) |

Flags:

| Flag | Value | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--root` | `<dir>` | no | extension root (inside a git work tree) |
| `--dry-run` | — | no | run every read and check, print the plan (files, commit message, push) and write nothing outside the cache |

Check ids:

| Id | Description | Levels |
|---|---|---|
| `post-merge-pr` | the PR's head is ext/<name> and it merged (N/A when open or closed unmerged) | PASS, FAIL, N/A, ERROR |
| `post-merge-rewrites` | raycastbot's trailing commits on the PR branch modified or added only files inside the extension | PASS, FAIL, N/A, ERROR |
| `post-merge-adopt` | every rewritten path is ALREADY, ADOPT or STAMP under the outcome table | PASS, FAIL, N/A, ERROR |
| `post-merge-signing` | the rx signing key exists and is registered on GitHub as a signing key | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A, ERROR |
| `post-merge-commit` | the signed cleanup commit, installed under git's index lock (under --dry-run, the planned one) | PASS, FAIL, N/A, ERROR |
| `post-merge-push` | the cleanup commit goes to the branch's single upstream URL as a one-commit fast-forward | PASS, WARN, N/A, ERROR |

Data (`--json` → `data`):

- `pr` — int — the pull request number used
- `merged` — boolean
- `mergeCommit` — string | null
- `branch` — string | null
- `rewrites` — [{ sha, files: string[] }] — raycastbot's trailing commits and the extension-relative files each changed
- `files` — [{ path, outcome: ADOPT | STAMP | ALREADY | FAIL, pre: string | null, post, head: string | null, index: string | null, work: string | null, reason: string | null }] — path extension-relative; the side values are blob ids
- `signingKey` — { path, created: boolean, registered: boolean | null } | null
- `commit` — string | null — the cleanup commit this run made
- `pushed` — { remote, branch } | null — the remote name and the merge ref pushed
- `dryRun` — boolean

## `rx pr`

verify a Store PR is yours, check its file set, and edit its body without clobbering hand edits

- Root: none
- Network: GitHub API via gh (raycast/extensions unless --repo)
- State: body: a copy of every live body read goes to the cross-repo cache pr-body/<owner>/<name>/<N>/<timestamp>.md; verify and files write nothing

Subcommands: `verify`, `files`, `body`.

### `rx pr verify`

author, head branch ext/<name>, draft, open and base raycast/extensions:main, each a result

Synopsis: `rx pr verify <N> --author <login> --extension <name> [--json]`

- Root: none
- Network: GitHub API via gh (raycast/extensions unless --repo)
- State: body: a copy of every live body read goes to the cross-repo cache pr-body/<owner>/<name>/<N>/<timestamp>.md; verify and files write nothing
- Preset: not accepted

Arguments:

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `<N>` | yes | pull request number in raycast/extensions |

Flags:

| Flag | Value | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--author` | `<login>` | yes | the GitHub login the PR must be authored by |
| `--extension` | `<name>` | yes | extension folder name; the head branch must be ext/<name> |

Check ids:

| Id | Description | Levels |
|---|---|---|
| `pr-author` | PR author login equals --author | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A, ERROR (default) |
| `pr-head` | head branch is ext/<extension> | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A, ERROR (default) |
| `pr-draft` | PR is still a draft | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A, ERROR (default) |
| `pr-open` | PR is open | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A, ERROR (default) |
| `pr-base` | base is raycast/extensions:main | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A, ERROR (default) |

Data (`--json` → `data`):

- `number` — int
- `author` — string
- `head` — string
- `base` — string owner/repo:ref
- `draft` — boolean
- `state` — string

### `rx pr files`

FAIL on any changed file outside extensions/<name>/ (rename sources included, all pages fetched); with --preset, FAIL on a local-only file the PR adds or changes

Synopsis: `rx pr files <N> --extension <name> [--preset <file>] [--json]`

- Root: none
- Network: GitHub API via gh (raycast/extensions unless --repo)
- State: body: a copy of every live body read goes to the cross-repo cache pr-body/<owner>/<name>/<N>/<timestamp>.md; verify and files write nothing
- Preset: preset-aware; the runner appends `--preset`

Arguments:

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `<N>` | yes | pull request number in raycast/extensions |

Flags:

| Flag | Value | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--extension` | `<name>` | yes | extension folder name |
| `--preset` | `<file>` | no | preset JSON, validated against the preset schema; reads holdout.localOnly for the pr-local-only check |

Check ids:

| Id | Description | Levels |
|---|---|---|
| `pr-files` | every changed path is under extensions/<extension>/ (details: each file with its GitHub status) | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A, ERROR (default) |
| `pr-local-only` | with --preset: every changed path the preset's holdout.localOnly lists (AGENTS.md, CONCEPTS.md, CLAUDE.md, HANDOFF.md, .env, …, under extensions/<extension>/) has status removed (PASS names the removals; FAIL any other status); N/A without --preset | PASS, FAIL, N/A |

Data (`--json` → `data`):

- `files` — [{ path, status, previous }] one per changed file: status is GitHub's (added, removed, modified, renamed, copied, changed, unchanged); previous is the rename source, else null
- `paths` — string[] every changed path, rename sources included
- `stray` — string[] paths outside the extension

### `rx pr body`

write the PR body onto the LIVE body: --initial first post only, --splice every later edit; dry run without --apply

Synopsis: `rx pr body <N> [--initial <file>] [--splice <file>] [--apply] [--prospective <file>] [--repo <owner/repo>] [--json]`

- Root: none
- Network: GitHub API via gh (raycast/extensions unless --repo)
- State: body: a copy of every live body read goes to the cross-repo cache pr-body/<owner>/<name>/<N>/<timestamp>.md; verify and files write nothing
- Preset: not accepted

Arguments:

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `<N>` | yes | pull request number |

Flags:

| Flag | Value | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--initial` | `<file>` | no | first post: the whole body, allowed only onto an unedited body carrying the template checklist |
| `--splice` | `<file>` | no | JSON [{ find, replace }]; each find is whole lines occurring exactly once in the live body |
| `--apply` | — | no | write (once); without it, print the diff and write nothing |
| `--prospective` | `<file>` | no | dry run: write the whole composed body to this file (outside the extension) for rx scan --pr-text; with --apply: refuse unless the body composed now equals that file byte for byte |
| `--repo` | `<owner/repo>` | no | repository (default raycast/extensions) |

Check ids:

| Id | Description | Levels |
|---|---|---|
| `pr-body-diff` | the proposed body was derived safely from the live body (diff in details); FAIL names the refused anchor or the edited body | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A, ERROR (default) |
| `pr-body-write` | the single PATCH landed and the edit history shows nothing was overwritten; N/A on a dry run or no change; FAIL (nothing written) when --apply --prospective names a file that differs from the body composed now | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A, ERROR (default) |

Data (`--json` → `data`):

- `applied` — boolean
- `before` — sha256:… of the live body read
- `after` — sha256:… of the body sent (or proposed)
- `edits` — int
- `overwritten` — boolean

## `rx preflight`

Store-readiness checks on an extension (core facts; preset-bound house rules with --preset)

Synopsis: `rx preflight [--root <dir>] [--published <dir>] [--preset <file>] [--extension-typescript] [--json]`

- Root: required
- Network: none
- State: none (read-only, and runs no code from the extension unless --extension-typescript is given); reads repo/stale/baseline.json for the `published` applicability value when present
- Preset: preset-aware; the runner appends `--preset`

Flags:

| Flag | Value | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--root` | `<dir>` | no | extension root |
| `--published` | `<dir>` | no | the extension as published in raycast/extensions (enables the comparison checks) |
| `--preset` | `<file>` | no | preset JSON (schema/preset.schema.json); without it preset-class checks are N/A |
| `--extension-typescript` | — | no | parse src/ with the extension's installed typescript, which loads and runs that package's code (as a build would); `rx gates` passes it. Without it the source is only read, by a text scan (shortcut-platform-case is then a WARN at most) |

Check ids:

| Id | Description | Levels |
|---|---|---|
| `package-json` | package.json parses and its list fields are arrays of objects | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A |
| `schema` | package.json $schema is Raycast's extension schema URL | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A |
| `categories` | at least one category from Raycast's list; Other only as a last resort (WARN) | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A |
| `platforms` | platforms is declared and contains only macOS and Windows (missing on main too → WARN) | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A |
| `preference-type` | every preference type is one Raycast defines | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A |
| `shortcut-platform-case` | shortcut platform keys are spelled macOS and Windows: with --extension-typescript (rx gates passes it) parsed with the extension's own typescript, and a miscased windows/macos key holding an object with both modifiers and key FAILs; without the flag, or with no loadable typescript, a text scan reports a WARN at most; a file that does not parse is a WARN that it was not fully checked | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A |
| `changelog-exists` | CHANGELOG.md exists | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A |
| `changelog-order` | changelog dates descend, are YYYY-MM-DD, and there is no Unreleased section; an inversion the published CHANGELOG already has (every published dated heading kept byte for byte, in order, the pair adjacent in both) is a WARN, since dated entries are not edited | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A |
| `changelog-updated` | with --published, the top changelog entry is new | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A |
| `command-renamed` | with --published, no published command name vanished (rename-shaped → FAIL, removal → WARN) | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A |
| `eslint-config` | flat ESLint config; no .eslintrc*; defineConfig from eslint/config | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A |
| `lockfile` | package-lock.json is the only lock file | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A |
| `npm-registry` | .npmrc and the lockfile resolve packages only from registry.npmjs.org | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A |
| `native-fetch` | no node-fetch / cross-fetch / isomorphic-fetch import | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A |
| `unused-dependencies` | every dependency is imported under src/ (FAIL); a package src/ appears to import at runtime but lists only in devDependencies is a heuristic WARN | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A |
| `readme-assets` | README images live in media/, not metadata/ or assets/ (Markdown-aware) | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A |
| `screenshots` | an extension with a view or menu-bar command has at least one PNG screenshot in metadata/ (a published extension whose only such commands are menu-bar ones → WARN) | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A |
| `launch-command` | heuristic: prefer launchCommand() over a raycast://extensions deeplink | PASS, WARN, N/A |
| `favicon` | heuristic: prefer getFavicon() over a hand-built favicon URL | PASS, WARN, N/A |
| `trash` | heuristic: prefer trash() over a shell command | PASS, WARN, N/A |
| `localization` | heuristic: no locale sniffing; Raycast is US English | PASS, WARN, N/A |
| `prettierrc` | .prettierrc matches the preset's values (and its import-sorting plugin pairs with devDependencies) | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A |
| `hand-typed-preferences` | no hand-written Preferences / Arguments types | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A |
| `title-case` | manifest titles are Title Case (heuristic) | PASS, WARN, N/A |
| `agent-scaffolding` | no agent or planning file the published copy lacks would ship (an edit to one already there is the owner's call); preset ship.keep exempts named paths | PASS, WARN, N/A |
| `dev-material` | no repo-only file (LICENSE, contributor docs, docs/, tools/) the published copy lacks would ship | PASS, WARN, N/A |
| `contributing-mirror` | a CONTRIBUTING.md stays in the mirror: the extension's .gitignore keeps it out of the Store PR, unless the published copy already ships one | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A |
| `generated-files` | no build output (dist/, .build/) would ship; a stray .DS_Store WARNs | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A |
| `screenshot-count` | at most 6 screenshots in metadata/ | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A |
| `screenshot-format` | only .png files under metadata/ | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A |
| `screenshot-size` | every screenshot is 2000×1250 | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A |
| `icon-size` | the extension icon (and PNG command icons) are 512×512 | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A |
| `store-description` | a new or changed package.json description is about 50 to 155 characters, ends with a period, has none of the shared filler, and names only listed platforms | PASS, WARN, N/A |
| `readme-dev-sections` | README has no Development, build-from-source, clone-and-run or project-structure section, nor a Scripts or Contributing section over contributor commands (the README is the Store page) | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A |
| `readme-links` | every relative link in README.md and docs/**/*.md resolves from its own directory to a file that ships | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A |
| `changelog-placeholder` | exactly one {PR_MERGE_DATE}, on the top changelog entry | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A |
| `script-utils` | AppleScript and JXA run through runAppleScript from @raycast/utils: no "osascript" string literal (an exec/spawn of the binary) and no run-applescript package under src/ (Greptile script-and-sql-utils) | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A |
| `failure-toast-helper` | parsed with the extension's TypeScript (--extension-typescript, as rx gates does): object-literal style: Toast.Style.Failure inside a catch block or first callback of .catch(), or in a function reached by one identifier call from those paths or passed by identifier as the first .catch() argument (lexically resolved local functions/arrows or named/aliased/default relative imports under src/, following relative barrel re-exports up to eight re-export edges with cycle detection); each style property reports once, syntax errors WARN as not fully inspected; without a compiler a text scan WARNs at most and labels its PASS; result toasts outside catch paths and progress-toast assignments pass; .then(ok, onRejected), object/class methods, namespace imports are out of scope; domain-action Failure toasts can be legitimate exceptions (Greptile failure-toasts) | PASS, WARN, N/A |
| `nested-review-config` | no nested Greptile config (.greptile/, greptile.json) at any depth would ship | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A |
| `pref-description-length` | preference descriptions within the preset's budget | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A |
| `pref-label-length` | preference labels within the preset's budget | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A |
| `logger` | the preset's logger package is a dependency, imported, with its checkbox preference declared | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A |
| `logger-verbose-copy` | the verboseLogging preference equals the preset's block, every field | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A |
| `logger-strict-redaction` | the strictRedaction preference equals the preset's block, every field | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A |
| `agents-md-paths` | every backticked repo path in AGENTS.md / CONCEPTS.md exists (repo file extensions only; <!-- rx-ignore agents-md --> exempts a line) | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A |
| `agents-md-scripts` | every `npm run <x>` in AGENTS.md / CONCEPTS.md is a package.json script (<!-- rx-ignore agents-md --> exempts a line) | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A |
| `agents-md-no-home-paths` | no home-directory path (a machine path under the user's home) in AGENTS.md / CONCEPTS.md | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A |
| `agents-md-symbols` | every backticked symbol() in AGENTS.md / CONCEPTS.md exists under src/ (<!-- rx-ignore agents-md --> exempts a line) | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A |

Data (`--json` → `data`):

- `root` — string
- `published` — boolean — whether --published was given
- `publishedDir` — string | null
- `preset` — string | null — the preset path
- `selfAuthored` — boolean | null — null without a preset
- `checks` — { [id]: "core" | "preset" }

## `rx preset`

validate a preset (check) or regenerate the audit matrix it describes (table)

- Root: none
- Network: none
- State: table rewrites the region between <!-- rx:matrix:start --> and <!-- rx:matrix:end --> in --into (compare only with --check)

Subcommands: `check`, `table`.

### `rx preset check`

schema, duplicate ids, anchors, bindings against their registries, severity downgrades

Synopsis: `rx preset check <file> [--json]`

- Root: none
- Network: none
- State: table rewrites the region between <!-- rx:matrix:start --> and <!-- rx:matrix:end --> in --into (compare only with --check)
- Preset: not accepted

Arguments:

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `<file>` | yes | preset JSON |

Check ids:

| Id | Description | Levels |
|---|---|---|
| `preset-schema` | valid against schema/preset.schema.json; unknown fields rejected | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A, ERROR (default) |
| `preset-ids` | no duplicate rule ids | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A, ERROR (default) |
| `preset-anchors` | every anchor resolves to a section in its reference file | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A, ERROR (default) |
| `preset-bindings` | a non-build rule has a binding; each binding exists in its own registry (rx checks, ESLint rules, judgment decisions) | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A, ERROR (default) |
| `preset-severity` | no report-severity rule binds a core check that would FAIL (it would downgrade a Store failure) | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A, ERROR (default) |

Data (`--json` → `data`):

- `rules` — number
- `bindings` — { rx, eslint, judgment }
- `errors` — string[]
- `eslintRegistry` — "present" | "absent"

### `rx preset table`

regenerate the audit matrix region in a reference file from the preset

Synopsis: `rx preset table <file> --into <reference.md> [--check] [--json]`

- Root: none
- Network: none
- State: table rewrites the region between <!-- rx:matrix:start --> and <!-- rx:matrix:end --> in --into (compare only with --check)
- Preset: not accepted

Arguments:

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `<file>` | yes | preset JSON |

Flags:

| Flag | Value | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--into` | `<reference.md>` | yes | the reference file holding the rx:matrix markers |
| `--check` | — | no | compare only; FAIL when the region differs |

Check ids:

| Id | Description | Levels |
|---|---|---|
| `preset-table` | the matrix region is written (or, with --check, identical) | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A, ERROR (default) |

Data (`--json` → `data`):

- `rows` — number
- `changed` — boolean

## `rx publication`

record which pull request and remote head a successful publish produced

- Root: none
- Network: none
- State: writes repo/publication.json (`git rev-parse --git-path rx` of the git repository containing --root, else the working directory)

Subcommands: `record`.

### `rx publication record`

write repo/publication.json { repo, pr, remoteSha, at } for `rx greptile can-reply --claims-fix`

Synopsis: `rx publication record <repo> <pr> <sha> [--root <dir>] [--json]`

- Root: none
- Network: none
- State: writes repo/publication.json (`git rev-parse --git-path rx` of the git repository containing --root, else the working directory)
- Preset: not accepted

Arguments:

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `<repo>` | yes | the repository the pull request is in, owner/name (raycast/extensions) |
| `<pr>` | yes | the pull request number, a positive integer |
| `<sha>` | yes | the remote head the publish produced: a full 40-hex lowercase commit SHA |

Flags:

| Flag | Value | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--root` | `<dir>` | no | any directory inside the git repository whose state holds the record (default: the working directory); no extension is needed |

Check ids:

| Id | Description | Levels |
|---|---|---|
| `publication-record` | the record was validated and written | PASS, ERROR |

Data (`--json` → `data`):

- `file` — absolute path of the record written
- `record` — { repo, pr, remoteSha, at }

## `rx scan`

gate −2: find forbidden example values in the payload, its file names, the commits ray publishes and PR text

Synopsis: `rx scan [--root <dir>] --forbidden <file> [--pr-text <file>]... [--json]`

- Root: required
- Network: none (reads git history locally)
- State: none
- Preset: not accepted

Flags:

| Flag | Value | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--root` | `<dir>` | no | extension root |
| `--forbidden` | `<file>` | yes | text file, one literal per line; blank lines and # comments ignored; keep it outside the extension root |
| `--pr-text` | `<file>` | no, repeatable | a PR body, comment or reply file to scan before sending |

Check ids:

| Id | Description | Levels |
|---|---|---|
| `scan-files` | no forbidden literal in any text file ray publish copies (symlinks read through; unreadable target → ERROR) | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A, ERROR (default) |
| `scan-names` | no forbidden literal in any payload path | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A, ERROR (default) |
| `scan-commits` | no forbidden literal in the commit messages ray publishes (HEAD...<publish tag>, else all history) | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A, ERROR (default) |
| `scan-pr-text` | no forbidden literal in any --pr-text file (N/A when none given) | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A, ERROR (default) |
| `scan-binary` | WARN listing binary payload files that need a human look; PASS when none | PASS, WARN, N/A |

Data (`--json` → `data`):

- `forbiddenHash` — "sha256:<hex>" of the forbidden file's bytes
- `forbiddenCount` — number of literals after dropping blank lines and comments
- `range` — the git log range scanned ("HEAD...<tag>" or "HEAD" for all history), or null when not a git work tree
- `hits` — total number of hit details across the four scans
- `binaries` — string[] — payload files skipped as binary

## `rx shortcuts`

runtime Keyboard.Shortcut.Common table from the installed Raycast app, and an extension's shortcuts checked against it

- Root: none
- Network: none
- State: none

Subcommands: `runtime`, `check`.

### `rx shortcuts runtime`

extract the Common table, app version and shim fingerprint from the installed Raycast app into the cache

Synopsis: `rx shortcuts runtime [--app <Raycast.app>] [--json]`

- Root: none
- Network: none (reads Raycast.app from /Applications or ~/Applications, or --app; `plutil` runs through execFile)
- State: writes $XDG_CACHE_HOME/raycast-harness/shortcuts/<shimFingerprint>.json
- Preset: not accepted

Flags:

| Flag | Value | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--app` | `<Raycast.app>` | no | the Raycast.app bundle to read instead of the one found in /Applications or ~/Applications |

Check ids:

| Id | Description | Levels |
|---|---|---|
| `shortcut-runtime-table` | a Keyboard.Shortcut.Common table from the running Raycast app is available (ERROR runtime evidence unavailable when shortcuts are declared and none matches; N/A only when none are declared) | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A, ERROR (default) |

Data (`--json` → `data`):

- `appVersion` — string | null — CFBundleShortVersionString of the installed app
- `shimFingerprint` — string — SHA-256 of the shim file the app loads
- `path` — string — the table file written
- `count` — number — Common constants in the table

### `rx shortcuts check`

compare the extension's resolved panels and toast actions with the runtime table

Synopsis: `rx shortcuts check [--table <file>] [--root <dir>] [--extension-typescript] [--json]`

- Root: required
- Network: none
- State: reads shortcuts/<shimFingerprint>.json from the cache (the fingerprint of the installed app's shim) unless --table is given; writes nothing; runs no code from the extension unless --extension-typescript is given
- Preset: not accepted

Flags:

| Flag | Value | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--table` | `<file>` | no | a table written by `rx shortcuts runtime` (or a recorded fixture) instead of the one matching the installed app |
| `--root` | `<dir>` | no | extension root |
| `--extension-typescript` | — | no | read source with the extension's installed typescript, which loads and runs that package's code (as a build would); without it the source is only read, by the text scan |

Check ids:

| Id | Description | Levels |
|---|---|---|
| `shortcut-runtime-table` | a Keyboard.Shortcut.Common table from the running Raycast app is available (ERROR runtime evidence unavailable when shortcuts are declared and none matches; N/A only when none are declared) | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A, ERROR (default) |
| `shortcut-ambiguous` | no two actions in one resolved ActionPanel (or one toast) share a binding on a declared platform; one FAIL per conflicting pair | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A, ERROR (default) |
| `shortcut-reserved` | no ActionPanel shortcut spells out a binding its view's panel assigns itself (↵ and ⌘↵ in List, Grid and Detail; ⌘↵ and ⌘⇧↵ in Form); one FAIL per site and distinct binding, or a WARN when rx cannot see the view and the binding is a default in only some views; toast actions are not panels and are not checked | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A, ERROR (default) |

Data (`--json` → `data`):

- `table` — { path, appVersion, shimFingerprint } | null
- `declared` — number — shortcuts found (resolved or not)
- `conflicts` — [{ platforms, binding, sites: [{ file, line, title, source }] }]
- `reserved` — [{ platforms, binding, why, certain, host, site }]
- `platforms` — the platforms package.json declares (absent → ["macOS"])
- `unresolved` — [{ file, line, title, source }] — declared shortcuts whose binding could not be read statically (a variable, a spread, a composed component; see src/shortcuts/scan.mjs)
- `groups` — { panels, toasts, loose }
- `files` — number of source files scanned
- `parser` — string | null — the extension's TypeScript the scan read source with ("typescript <version>"); null without --extension-typescript or when none could be loaded
- `textScanned` — string[] — files read by the fallback text scan instead (every file without a parser, else those that did not parse cleanly)

## `rx stale`

compare the local extension with its published copy in raycast/extensions, path by path

Synopsis: `rx stale [--root <dir>] [--preset <file>] [--json]`

- Root: required
- Network: GitHub API (publication lookup) and `git fetch` of raycast/extensions into the cross-repo cache
- State: reads/writes cache/upstream/ (sparse checkout); writes repo/stale/baseline.json { name, published, baseline, at } (no cache path)
- Preset: preset-aware; the runner appends `--preset`

Flags:

| Flag | Value | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--root` | `<dir>` | no | extension root |
| `--preset` | `<file>` | no | preset JSON, validated against the preset schema; reads holdout.localOnly so a listed path the published copy has and local lacks is REMOVE (a deliberate deletion), not ONLY-PUB |

Check ids:

| Id | Description | Levels |
|---|---|---|
| `stale` | N/A when the extension is not published (no baseline to compare) | N/A |
| `stale-mine` | published == local HEAD for these paths (PASS) | PASS |
| `stale-check` | published == an older commit of these paths; WARN requiring an audit disposition | WARN |
| `stale-new` | local files the published tree lacks; WARN requiring an audit disposition | WARN |
| `stale-upstream` | published content not in these paths' history (FAIL) | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A, ERROR (default) |
| `stale-only-pub` | published files local lacks and never had at that path in its reachable history; publishing deletes them (FAIL) | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A, ERROR (default) |
| `stale-remove` | published files the preset's holdout.localOnly lists and local lacks (held out by rx holdout, or absent); publishing deletes them on purpose; WARN requiring an audit disposition remove-published | WARN |
| `stale-deleted` | published files local deleted (in the working tree or an unreleased commit) whose published blob is at that path in a commit reachable from local HEAD; publishing deletes them; WARN requiring an audit disposition remove-published | WARN |
| `stale-unhandled` | symlink, mode change or undecidable path (FAIL) | PASS, FAIL, WARN, N/A, ERROR (default) |

Data (`--json` → `data`):

- `name` — string — package.json name
- `published` — boolean
- `publishedDir` — string | null — cache path of the published copy (a convenience for this run; never persisted)
- `baseline` — string | null — raycast/extensions main commit the comparison used
- `files` — [{ path, class, localHash, publishedHash | null, note }] — class ∈ MINE CHECK NEW? UPSTREAM ONLY-PUB REMOVE DELETED UNHANDLED; localHash is the git blob id of the on-disk bytes (null when absent locally; a REMOVE or DELETED disposition keys it as "absent")
